title: Inventory Information Frictions Explain Price Rigidity in Perishable Groceries
eligible_reason: No regression is estimated anywhere in the package (the regression extractor found zero commands). The empirical pilot section compares a single treated store (EU store, electronic shelf labels and expanded barcodes installed once) against a synthetic-control-style comparison built from the UK store: code/generate_synthetic_control_figure.R draws 1,000 (paper: 100,000) random 23-product subsets of the 97 UK products, picks the subset minimizing the pre-period Euclidean distance in weekly price changes per SKU, and plots the two series (Figure 7). One treated unit, one adoption date, no fixed-effects regression, and a synthetic-control comparison: fails the staggered-binary-treatment, two-cohort, and TWFE requirements. The shipped data are simulated (readme: 'Our data are subject to an NDA, so we offer a simulated data generator').
design_notes: Store-product-week panel of price-change counts for two stores. UK store: 97 perishable products, weeks -20..20 around installation; EU store: 23 products, weeks -51..49 around installation. Treatment = installation of electronic shelf labels and expanded barcodes in the EU store (post = week > 0); the UK store serves as the comparison pool. The only 'design' is a before/after plot of the EU store against the best-matching UK subsample. The 'ft_staggered' flag that put the paper in the frame is unrelated to a staggered-adoption DiD (the paper is a theory/structural paper on price rigidity with a two-store empirical pilot). Data are generated by code/generate_simulated_data.R to match reported moments (Poisson means 0.534/0.551 for UK pre/post, 0.55/5.26 for EU pre/post).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: One treated store (EU) with one installation date; the UK store is never treated within the analysis window.
data_files_note: data/simulated_price_change_data.rds (161 KB, R rds; store, product, week, price_change). Simulated by code/generate_simulated_data.R; real transaction data under NDA and not shipped. output/syntheticontrol.png is the generated figure.
software_note: R (data.table, tidyverse, ggplot2, extrafont, rstudioapi); two scripts.
screener_notes: Not a DiD/event-study regression paper. Single treated unit, single adoption date, synthetic-control-style comparison, simulated data only. Exclude.
